proposals.impact: restores automated content publishing; queue is at 1 post, so failures compound daily
proposals.observation: Three CI workflows failed on 2026-07-27: Daily Blog Post (06:41), Weekly Monday Report (08:58), and Funnel-Hack Digest (11:57). The content queue shows only 1 post queued and 47 published. With automated publishing broken, new content stops reaching subscribers entirely. The Money Vigilance automation is converting at 66.67% open rate, which means warmed subscribers exist, but the top-of-funnel content feed that drives new quiz entries and email sign-ups has gone quiet.
proposals.proposal:
Inspect the Daily Blog Post workflow logs to find the failure reason (most likely a missing API key, a changed content schema after the recent content.config.ts work, or a jsPDF-related dependency bump in package.json that shifted a peer dependency). Fix the root cause in the workflow YAML or the called script. The Weekly Monday Report and Funnel-Hack Digest failures on the same day suggest a shared upstream cause, so fixing the blog post workflow first will likely surface whether it is a credentials or schema issue that cascades to the others.

This is the single highest-leverage action because every other channel (email automations, quiz, booking) depends on a steady content feed to bring in cold traffic. One file edit to the workflow YAML, or one environment secret rotation, unblocks all three.
proposals.new_text:
# Diagnosis step — run this in your terminal before editing the YAML:
# gh run view --log-failed <run-id-for-daily-blog-post>
#
# Common fix pattern if the failure is a missing or rotated secret:
# 1. Go to repo Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions
# 2. Rotate MAILERLITE_API_KEY (or whichever secret the log flags as undefined)
# 3. Re-run the failed workflow from the GitHub Actions UI
#
# If the log shows a schema validation error after the recent content.config.ts
# changes, the fix is to update the frontmatter defaults in the workflow's
# post-generation script to match the new schema fields.
#
# Add this debug step to the workflow temporarily to expose the exact error:
#
#      - name: Debug env
#        run: env | grep -i api | sed 's/=.*/=***/'

proposals.impact: 66.67% open rate shows highest engagement; optimising subject line for emails 2+ could lift opens on the weakest automation (Money Worship at 37.5%)
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has a 66.67% open rate across 12 sends. Money Worship sits at 37.5% across 16 sends. These two automations serve subscribers who scored into different money-script profiles from the same quiz. The gap of 29 percentage points between the best and worst performing automation is too large to explain by audience quality alone. The most likely cause is that the Money Worship subject line is either too generic or not specific enough to the thing that Money Worship subscribers actually feel day-to-day.
proposals.proposal:
Rewrite the subject line of Email 1 in the Money Worship automation. Money Worship subscribers tend to believe money will solve everything and then feel shame or deflation when it does not. The current subject line (unknown, but performing at 37.5%) is not landing that specific tension. A subject line grounded in the felt experience, not the label, will close the gap.

The new subject line below is written to pass the Sultanic test: a subscriber who earns well but still feels behind would recognise this sentence as their own internal monologue, not a coach's category name.
proposals.new_text: subject: "You earn more than you used to. The dread didn't leave, did it."

proposals.impact: quiz has zero starts in 48h; adding a single in-content CTA pointing to it from the highest-traffic recent post could restart the funnel
proposals.observation: The quiz shows zero sessions and zero starts across the full 48-hour window. The three most recent blog posts, published in June 2026, cover topics that map directly to quiz entry points: buying courses compulsively, avoiding money goals, and comparing yourself to peers. Each of these posts ends without a link to the quiz. Readers who finish those posts and feel recognised have nowhere to go except away.
proposals.proposal: Add a single in-content CTA block at the bottom of the most recent blog post ("Why do I keep buying courses and planners hoping THIS one finally fixes everything?") pointing to the quiz. The copy needs to feel like a natural continuation of the post, not a sales insert. The post is about compulsive course-buying, so the CTA should name the pattern the reader just read about and offer the quiz as a way to look at what is underneath it, not fix it.
